envelope.description: Resolve and pass the range base in the validate and completion writers

body.title: Resolve and pass the range base in the validate and completion writers
body.summary: Have both writers resolve the base — stamped meta.rangeBase first, then the PLAN-introducing commit as fallback for the already-written records that predate the stamp — and pass it to the widened collector. If NEITHER resolves: log and return an EMPTY change set. Never throw, never substitute a different range. This is where the approved design explicitly diverges from the shipped code-review chain (c12), which falls back to HEAD^ and then the empty-tree object; a populated wrong answer is worse than an honest absence. s1 established that the trivial route has NO upstream artifact at all, so for a trivial build both sources are legitimately unavailable and empty is the correct, specified outcome rather than a failure — stated explicitly so it is not met as a surprise. CRITIQUE APPLIED, twice: re-sized M->L, because the PLAN-commit fallback requires deriving an artifact path from epicHash plus storyId and running a `git log --diff-filter=A` lookup against it — machinery that exists nowhere today — and the build should budget for it rather than discover it mid-task; and t1 added to dependsOn, since this task INVERTS t1's TEST C and an inversion performed against a test whose authoring task was never declared is how a characterisation gets quietly deleted instead of flipped.
acceptanceChecks: A CLEAN working tree with a stamped base yields every file changed across base..HEAD — the test that fails before this task and is the point of the Story, INVERTING t1's TEST C, which is rewritten here rather than deleted

A CLEAN tree with NO base and no resolvable PLAN commit yields an EMPTY set, NOT the last commit's files — pinning the deliberate divergence from the HEAD^ chain so a later 'helpful' fallback cannot slip in unnoticed
A DIRTY tree yields exactly today's result and never consults the base — asserted via a recording seam, proving independence from the commit/validate ordering
A multi-task Story's change set GROWS across tasks rather than describing only the latest
A legacy record with no stamped base resolves via the PLAN-introducing commit, reproducing the method used in the bfe98ff7 s4 repair
An APPROVED-BUT-UNCOMMITTED PLAN yields empty rather than an error — the state this very Story's LLD was in when the base question was resolved, so the case is real rather than theoretical
An unresolvable base LOGS and returns empty; the record is still written and the build is NOT blocked
A trivial-route build, having no plan and no LLD to stamp, yields an empty change set without error
BOTH writers resolve the base identically — the validate phase and the completion-time writer share one resolver rather than each implementing the chain
